name: JavaScript
description: Writing modern JavaScript, including types, functions, closures, arrays and asynchronous code with promises and async/await.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const creates a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned (though an object it refers to can still be mutated).

questions.question: What does typeof null evaluate to?
questions.explanation: typeof null is "object", a long-standing quirk kept for backward compatibility.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].map(x => x * 2) return?
questions.explanation: map returns a new array containing the callback's result for each element.

questions.question: How does === differ from ==?
options: === compares without type coercion; == converts types before comparing
questions.explanation: For example 0 == '0' is true but 0 === '0' is false.

questions.question: What order is printed by: console.log('A'); setTimeout(() => console.log('B'), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log('C')); console.log('D');
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs first (A, D); then the microtask queue (promise callback C) drains before the next macrotask (timer B).

questions.question: What does this print: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { setTimeout(() => console.log(i)); }
questions.explanation: var is function-scoped, so all callbacks share one i, which is 3 when they run; using let would print 0 1 2.

practical.title: Fetch a user's name
practical.instructions: Write an async JavaScript function getUserName(id) that fetches https://api.example.com/users/{id}, throws an Error if the response is not OK, and returns the name property from the JSON body.
practical.expected_output: async function getUserName(id) { const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/users/${id}`); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(...); const data = await res.json(); return data.name; }

rubric.hint: Mark the function async so you can use await.
Use await fetch(url) to get the Response.
fetch does not reject on HTTP errors; check response.ok and throw.
Call await response.json() to parse the body.

tasks.title: Learn JavaScript fundamentals
tasks.description: Work through the JavaScript Fundamentals part of javascript.info: variables, types, operators, conditionals, loops and functions. Run each example in the browser console or Node.
tasks.completion_criteria: All chapter tasks in the Fundamentals section attempted and solved.

tasks.title: Practise arrays, objects and string methods
tasks.description: Solve 10 small exercises using map, filter, reduce, object destructuring and template literals, such as grouping a list of people by age.

tasks.title: Master closures and async code
tasks.description: Study closures, promises, async/await and the event loop on javascript.info. Write a script that fetches data from two public APIs in parallel with Promise.all and handles errors.
tasks.completion_criteria: Script fetches in parallel, handles a failed request gracefully and you can explain microtasks vs macrotasks.

tasks.title: Build an interactive web app in vanilla JavaScript
tasks.description: Build a small app (e.g. a weather dashboard or quiz) in plain JavaScript that calls a public API, manipulates the DOM, stores preferences in localStorage and is organised into ES modules.
tasks.completion_criteria: Deployed app that loads live data, handles API errors and persists user preferences.
